highlight.title: Next.js 15.1 with React 19 Stable Support
highlight.summary: Next.js 15.1 officially brings stable React 19 support to both App and Pages routers, ending the RC phase. The update includes the stable 'after' API for post-response streaming execution and new forbidden/unauthorized APIs for granular auth handling.

resources.title: React 19 Server Actions + TypeScript: Complete Form Pattern Guide
resources.why_now: React 19's Actions API with useActionState hook eliminates 98% of form boilerplate while providing built-in TypeScript support. This represents a fundamental shift from manual state management to declarative server-side form handling.

resources.title: tRPC v11 + Server Components: The 2026 Full-Stack TypeScript Architecture
resources.why_now: tRPC v11 adapts to the Server Components era with server-invokable patterns that maintain type safety while enabling direct RSC calls. Critical for teams building complex dashboards that need both SSR and rich client interactions.

resources.title: Drizzle ORM vs Prisma: The TypeScript Performance Battle
resources.why_now: Drizzle ORM is becoming the preferred choice for serverless TypeScript apps due to smaller bundle sizes and faster cold starts. The shift from Prisma represents a maturation toward edge-first database patterns.

resources.title: Full-Stack TypeScript Patterns: Shared Types and Monorepo Architecture
resources.why_now: Modern TypeScript apps are consolidating around single-codebase patterns using frameworks like Next.js and TanStack Start. This approach reduces interface maintenance while keeping UI and API changes aligned through shared type systems.

claude_take: The React/Next.js ecosystem is reaching a stability inflection point where experimental features (Server Components, Actions) are becoming production-ready, while the TypeScript tooling has matured enough to support true end-to-end type safety from database to UI. This convergence makes 2026 the year where full-stack TypeScript moves from 'nice-to-have' to 'table stakes' for serious web applications.
